findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than restricting it to the VPC. Combined with a weak default 'admin' username, this greatly expands attack surface for the database.
storage_encrypted = false means the RDS instance's underlying storage, snapshots, and backups are stored unencrypted, exposing data if the storage layer or a snapshot is accessed.

The master password is supplied via var.password and the same variable is interpolated into EC2 user data; the password will also be stored in cleartext in Terraform state. No secrets manager or managed master password is used.

IAM database authentication is not enabled and a static master password with the predictable username 'admin' is used, leaving the publicly accessible database dependent solely on a shared static credential.

The user_data script writes the RDS master username and password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc in cleartext. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by anyone who can reach the instance (e.g. via SSRF) and is visible in the console/API to anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required", so IMDSv1 is allowed. A web application on this instance is a prime SSRF target, and IMDSv1 lets an attacker steal the instance profile credentials for the overly permissive ec2role.
The instance does not specify root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root volume (which stores the cleartext DB credentials file) may be created unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is attached to an internet-facing web server, so credential theft via SSRF/IMDS yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2, and RDS across the account, including privilege escalation paths.
Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database tier.

The security group has no description and relies on separate rules; more importantly, it is attached to a publicly accessible RDS instance, so the VPC-scoped ingress rule does not actually limit exposure introduced by the public endpoint.
The parameter group does not enforce require_secure_transport (TLS) for MySQL connections, so the publicly reachable database can accept unencrypted client connections carrying credentials and data.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set parameters and omits require_secure_transport = 1, permitting cleartext client connections to the database.
